stem.text: Determine whether the series \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n \), where \( a_n = \frac{5}{n^{2} + 6} \), converges or diverges. Name the test used and verify its conditions.

answer_key.label: The series converges by the direct comparison test, because \( 0 < a_n < \frac{5}{n^{2}} \text{ and } p = 2 > 1 \).

worked_solution.text: The terms are positive, so the direct comparison test applies. Compare with \( \sum \frac{5}{n^{2}} \), a multiple of the p-series with \( p = 2 \).
Adding \( 6 \) to the denominator makes each term smaller, so \( 0 < \frac{5}{n^{2} + 6} < \frac{5}{n^{2}} \) for every n.
The series converges by the direct comparison test, because \( 0 < a_n < \frac{5}{n^{2}} \text{ and } p = 2 > 1 \), so \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n \) converges.

options.label: The series converges by the nth term test, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} a_n = 0 \).
options.derivation: the verdict drawn from the terms approaching 0, which no test supports

options.label: The series diverges by the direct comparison test, because \( 0 < a_n < \frac{5}{n^{2}} \text{ and } p = 2 > 1 \).
options.derivation: the p-series threshold reversed, so the comparison series with p greater than 1 read as divergent
